problem: LocalGarage.destroy() unconditionally detaches the shared io-garage container from the branch network, but WP5 made buckets per-service, so destroying ONE bucket breaks S3 for every other bucket on that branch — and makes multi-bucket branch/project teardown leak buckets and objects.
evidence: src/adapters/garage.ts:219 `await docker(['network','disconnect', network, GARAGE])` runs on every destroy. Callers are now per-service, not per-branch: src/engine.ts:2978 (removeStorageService, one call per branch), src/engine.ts:2953 (addStorageService rollback), src/engine.ts:227 (provisionBranch rollback) and src/engine.ts:1600 (teardownBranch, one call per storage service). Consequences: (a) `DELETE /projects/:id/services/st-a` on a branch that also has st-b leaves the branch network without io-garage, so st-b's apps can no longer resolve the `http://io-garage:3900` endpoint minted in their env (src/adapters/garage.ts:195) — nothing re-attaches except a later storage provision (garage.ts:177 is the only `network connect`); (b) in teardownBranch the first destroy detaches garage, so the second bucket's `rclone purge` (garage.ts:214, run with `--network <branch net>`) can no longer reach garage and fails silently, then `bucket delete` of a non-empty bucket fails too (garage.ts:215), so the bucket and its objects leak while the teardown counter only records `failed`.
fix: Make the detach the branch's last step, not the bucket's: delete garage.ts:219 from `destroy()`, add an explicit detach step (e.g. `async detachFrom(network) { await docker(['network','disconnect', network, GARAGE]).catch(() => {}) }` on LocalGarage, optional on StorageAdapter) and call it once in `teardownBranch` (src/engine.ts, after the storage loop and before `docker network rm`) and in `removeStorageService`/the add-rollback only when `Object.keys(branch.buckets ?? {}).length === 0` after the row is dropped. Add a fake-adapter case in test/server.test.ts region WP5 that removes one of two storage services and asserts the other branch bucket is still reachable (recorded detach not called).

problem: `GET /projects/:id/secrets` still returns the container-only DSN for postgres, so the host-facing bundle the CLI injects (`insta run`, `insta secrets` → .env) carries a DATABASE_URL that does not resolve on the host. Plan 05 §5 specifies the lane form for dbSecretsFor and WP2's `laneAddress` has landed.
evidence: src/engine.ts:2647-2657 `dbSecretsFor` writes `row.url` (the stored `postgres://postgres:pw@io-<ref>-pg-<name>:5432/app`) for both `DATABASE_URL_<SUFFIX>` and the canonical alias, while `credentialsOn` for the same service does rewrite it through the lane (src/engine.ts:2733 `this.laneUrl(...)`). Plan 05 §5: \"dbSecretsFor (each dbServices entry in creation order: DATABASE_URL_<SUFFIX> = lane-form URL; the oldest also DATABASE_URL) ... Lane rewriting is WP2's laneAddress; until WP2 lands the stored container-host URL is returned unchanged.\" Contract 00 §10 row \"DATABASE_URL (secrets, credentials, env)\" requires the lane form in both modes. Impact path: insta-cli src/commands/run.ts:37 reads `GET /projects/:id/secrets` and injects it into a HOST process (docs/reference/cli/overview.mdx:140 \"Run a command with the branch credential bundle injected\"), so `insta run npm start` gets `io-demo-main-pg-db:5432`. The same seam is unconverted for managed databases (src/engine.ts:571-584 uses `managedContainerName(...)` instead of the landed `laneBundle(type, laneHost, lanePort, pw, tls)` in src/manageddb.ts:112).
fix: In `dbSecretsFor` return `this.laneUrl(project, branch, d.id, row.url)`; in `managedSecretsFor` build the bundle with `laneBundle(m.type, lane.host, lane.port, cred.password, lane.tls)` from `this.laneAddress(project, branch, m.id)`. `deployLocked` already wraps the result in `containerize()` (src/engine.ts:492), which maps 127.0.0.1 → host.docker.internal for containers, so container reachability is preserved. This changes assertions the scaffold pinned outside WP5's allowed-edit list — test/server.test.ts:94, 972-976, 994, 1025-1027, 1229, 1258, 1338 and WP5's own 1745-1747 — so the integrator has to sign the change off (or amend contract §10 to say secrets/env stay container-form while credentials are lane-form, which is what the code currently does).

problem: `TemplateExecutor.finish()` does not check the claim token that every other write in the run checks, so a run stranded past the 10-minute lease can mark a freshly started re-run of the same deploymentId as failed/partial while it is still creating services.
evidence: src/templates/executor.ts:364-372 `save()` refuses to write when `row.claimToken !== record.claimToken`, but src/templates/executor.ts:549-558 `finish()` mutates `r.status`/`r.error`/`r.logsTail` with no such guard. Reachable because `create()` starts a second run once `Date.now() - Date.parse(existing.updatedAt) >= RUN_LEASE_MS` (executor.ts:144) while run #1 is still alive — a multi-service manifest can exceed 10 minutes on its own (awaitDbReady + awaitHealthy are each bounded by `cfg.templates.healthTimeoutMs`, executor.ts:577 and 598, per service), and a `deploy` blocked on the per-key op lock has no bound at all.
fix: Give `finish` the token: `private finish(id: string, status, error, logTail, claimToken?: string)` and inside the mutate add `if (claimToken !== undefined && r.claimToken !== claimToken) return`. Pass `record.claimToken` from every call inside `run()` (executor.ts:458, 476, 497, 500, 504) and keep `abandonStale()` (executor.ts:101) passing the row's own `r.claimToken`.

problem: The public, unauthenticated `GET /templates` clones the whole state file once per template: `stats()` calls `loadState()` (a full structuredClone, including up to EVENTS_CAP = 5000 events) inside the listing map.
evidence: src/templates/catalog.ts:215 `const state = loadState()` inside `stats(code)`, invoked per entry at src/templates/catalog.ts:265 (`const s = this.stats(e.manifest.code)`) and again at :302 for the detail route — 7 clones per listing request today. `loadState` is documented as clone-per-call and \"Never on the router's request path\" (src/state.ts:98-99), and the route is on the server-mode public allowlist (src/auth.ts:31), so an anonymous caller drives the amplification.
fix: Read the state once per request and thread it through: change `stats(code: string, state = loadState())` and `isLive(row, projects)` callers so `listTemplates` does `const state = loadState()` before the map and passes it to every `this.stats(code, state)`; `getTemplate` does the same.

problem: A template's `meta.logo` is joined onto the template directory without a containment check, so a manifest can make the public catalog route embed any `.png`/`.svg` the daemon can read.
evidence: src/templates/catalog.ts:197-209: `const candidates = declared ? [declared.replace(/^\\.\\//, '')] : LOGO_FALLBACKS` then `readFileSync(join(base, rel))` and the bytes are returned as a `data:` URI on `GET /templates` / `GET /templates/:code`. The parser only type-checks the field (src/templates/manifest.ts:408-410 `scalarString(doc.meta[key], 'meta.logo')`), so `meta.logo: ../../../../home/user/keys.png` is accepted. The trust boundary is real because `cfg.templatesDir` is operator-settable (INSTA_OSS_TEMPLATES_DIR) and third-party template directories are the documented way to add templates.
fix: Constrain the path in `logo()`: reject a declared value that is absolute or contains a `..` segment, and verify containment before reading — `const p = resolve(base, rel); if (!p.startsWith(resolve(base) + sep)) continue`. Add a `refuses(...)` case for `meta.logo` traversal to test/templates.test.ts.

problem: Two templates.test.ts cases do not test what their names claim, leaving the two behaviours plan 05 lists uncovered: the log-tail redaction (untested anywhere) and the off-origin healthcheck refusal (the case actually asserts a probe DID run against a same-origin path).
evidence: test/templates.test.ts:337 'a health failure fails the run, names the last status and redacts the log tail' asserts only `status`, `step`, `error` and the event kind — never `view.logsTail`; the mocked docker logs payload (test/templates.test.ts:341) contains no secret to redact. `grep -rn \"redactLogTail\\|capLogTail\\|logsTail\" test/` returns nothing, so src/templates/manifest.ts:662 `redactLogTail` and :676 `capLogTail` — the guard that keeps generated secrets out of the durable row served by `GET /template-deployments/:id` — have no test at all. test/templates.test.ts:353 'a 401 counts as healthy; an off-origin healthcheck is refused without a probe' ends at line 365 with `expect(probed.length).toBeGreaterThan(before)` on a manifest whose healthcheck is `/ok` (same origin), so the refusal branch at src/templates/executor.ts:618 is never exercised. Plan 05 Tests requires \"logsTail present with the generated key redacted\" and \"off-origin healthcheck refused without a probe\".
fix: In the health-failure case, read the generated key first (`(await get('/projects/'+id+'/secrets?branch=main')).json().secrets.N8N_ENCRYPTION_KEY`, as the idempotency case at line 375 does), have the docker `logs` mock echo it, then assert `view.logsTail` contains `[redacted]` and `not.toContain(key)`. For the off-origin half, either drive `awaitHealthy` with an entry whose `healthcheck` is absolute (the branch is unreachable through the parser, so a direct executor-level case is the only way) and assert `probed.length === before` plus the 'refusing to probe it' reason, or drop that clause from the test name.

problem: `DELETE /projects/:id/services/cp-<unknown>` answers 200 with an empty teardown instead of 404, so the new teardown envelope reports a successful removal of a service that never existed.
evidence: src/server.ts:662-672 routes any `cp-` sid to `engine.removeComputeService(id, sid.slice(3))`, and src/engine.ts:1173-1197 never validates the name: the per-branch loop skips (`if (!b.apps[name]) continue`), the final mutate filters nothing, and it returns `{destroyed: 0, failed: 0}`. Contract 00 §9 documents `200 { teardown }; 404` for this route, and plan 05's own test bullet says \"unknown ids 404\"; test/server.test.ts:267 only covers `pg-ghost` (which throws in removeDbService).
fix: At the top of `removeComputeService`, after the project lookup: `if (!this.computeGroupNames(projectId).includes(name)) throw new Error('service not found')`, and extend test/server.test.ts:267 with `DELETE /projects/<id>/services/cp-ghost` expecting 404.

problem: Docs fact 2 of plan 05 (the canonical-alias plus suffixed-name rule for minted credentials) never reached the docs, so the user-visible naming rule behind `insta secrets` with several services of a type is undocumented.
evidence: Plan 05 \"Docs facts for WP8\": \"the oldest service of a type holds the canonical env alias (DATABASE_URL, BUCKET_NAME, ...), every service also has suffixed names (DATABASE_URL_ANALYTICS)\". `grep -rn 'DATABASE_URL_\\|alias\\|suffix' docs COMPATIBILITY.md README.md` finds nothing on this rule; COMPATIBILITY.md:22 documents only the per-type cap and one container/bucket per service, and docs/postgres/overview.mdx:17 mentions only `insta db url` and `insta secrets bind`. The behaviour itself is implemented and tested (src/engine.ts:2647-2670, test/server.test.ts:1741-1762).
fix: Add one line to the `secrets` row of COMPATIBILITY.md and to docs/postgres/overview.mdx: the oldest service of each type carries the unsuffixed keys (`DATABASE_URL`, the `AWS_*`/`BUCKET_NAME` bundle, `REDIS_URL`, ...), every service also gets `<KEY>_<NAME>` (`DATABASE_URL_ANALYTICS`), and removing the oldest shifts the unsuffixed keys onto the next one.

problem: WP3's own Docker suite cannot even be imported: test/sleep-wake.int.test.ts builds its config with INSTA_OSS_RAM_FLOOR_PCT='0', but the contract pins that knob to 1..90 and loadConfig throws on 0, so the file dies at module evaluation and none of its four cases ever run for the integrator.
evidence: test/sleep-wake.int.test.ts:39-49 (`loadConfig({... INSTA_OSS_RAM_FLOOR_PCT: '0' ...})` at module top level, outside any test) vs src/config.ts:247 (`ramFloorPct: int(env, 'INSTA_OSS_RAM_FLOOR_PCT', 15, 1, 90)`) and src/config.ts:120-124 (throws ConfigError when n < min). 00-contract.md:190 pins `15 (1..90)`. vitest.config.ts:14 includes test/**/*.int.test.ts as soon as RUN_DOCKER_TESTS is set. Reproduced: loadConfig({INSTA_OSS_MODE:'local',INSTA_OSS_DATA_DIR:'/tmp/x',INSTA_OSS_RAM_FLOOR_PCT:'0'}) -> \"INSTA_OSS_RAM_FLOOR_PCT must be an integer in 1..90 (got \\\"0\\\")\". Plan 03 \"Done when\" line 143 prescribes the same illegal 0.
fix: Keep the contract's bound and make the suite legal: in test/sleep-wake.int.test.ts set `INSTA_OSS_RAM_FLOOR_PCT: '1'` plus `INSTA_OSS_MEM_BUDGET_MB: '1048576'` (a synthetic 1 TiB total, so `available - need` can never fall under the 1% floor and no pressure pass can touch the containers under test), and fix the header comment at lines 14-17, which also claims `INSTA_OSS_SCHEDULER` is unset (line 42 sets '1') and describes an eviction case the file does not contain. If 0 is genuinely wanted, that is a contract edit (00-contract.md:190) plus a `ramFloorPct <= 0 -> return` guard at the top of evictForRoom, not just a wider bound.

problem: Pressure eviction has no off switch, and the shipped docs promise one that breaks the daemon. docs/self-hosting/sleep.mdx tells operators INSTA_OSS_RAM_FLOOR_PCT=0 disables eviction; that value makes loadConfig throw, so the daemon refuses to start. INSTA_OSS_SCHEDULER=0 is not a substitute either: it only skips the ticker, while evictForRoom is still called on every wake onto a stopped container, with no `cfg.sleep.enabled` check.
evidence: docs/self-hosting/sleep.mdx:115 (`| INSTA_OSS_RAM_FLOOR_PCT | 15 | free-memory floor for pressure eviction, 0 disables it |`) vs src/config.ts:247 + 120-124 (0 rejected). src/scheduler.ts:319-326 (`start()` only gates the setInterval on `cfg.sleep.enabled`) and src/scheduler.ts:536-542 (wakeLocked calls `this.evictForRoom(need, new Set([key]))` unconditionally), while src/scheduler.ts:453-460 has no floor/enabled short-circuit. Plan 03's Done-when reason for setting SCHEDULER=0 in Docker suites is precisely \"the pressure pass ... on a low-RAM runner stops the containers under test\", which SCHEDULER=0 does not achieve for the wake path: any `lifecycle start` / `ensurePgAwake` wake onto an exited container on a runner below 15% free will docker-stop one of the suite's own running services.
fix: Add the kill switch and make the doc true. In src/scheduler.ts:453, first line of evictForRoom: `if (!this.cfg.sleep.enabled || this.cfg.sleep.ramFloorPct <= 0) return` (the `enabled` half makes INSTA_OSS_SCHEDULER=0 mean \"no pressure pass anywhere\", which is what decision 12 says it means). Then either widen src/config.ts:247 to `int(env, 'INSTA_OSS_RAM_FLOOR_PCT', 15, 0, 90)` and amend 00-contract.md:190 to `15 (0..90, 0 disables)`, or, if the contract stays at 1..90, change docs/self-hosting/sleep.mdx:115 to say the accepted range is 1 to 90 and that INSTA_OSS_SCHEDULER=0 is how eviction is turned off.

problem: evictForRoom's loop cannot observe the memory it just freed when the runtime answers from the synthetic budget, so one pressure pass sleeps EVERY eligible service instead of the least recently active one. DockerRuntime.memory() in budget mode returns `budget - lastRssTotal`, and lastRssTotal is only recomputed inside stats(), which the sweep calls once before the pass and the wake path never calls. The loop's `tried` set is the only thing that stops it, i.e. it stops after draining the whole victim pool.
evidence: src/scheduler.ts:453-478 (loop re-reads `this.runtime.memory()` at 459 and returns only when `mem.availableBytes - needBytes >= floor` at 461; every iteration adds the victim to `tried` at 476 and sleeps it at 477) against src/scheduler.ts:610-616 (`memory()`: `availableBytes: Math.max(0, totalBytes - this.lastRssTotal)`) and src/scheduler.ts:595-607 (`lastRssTotal` assigned only in `stats()`). The fake-adapter suite hides this: test/scheduler.test.ts:501-503 monkey-patches `h.runtime.stop` to call `pressure(h, 250)` so that memory improves, and test/scheduler.test.ts:530-548 only avoids a stampede because the other candidates are protected. This is the documented macOS/local eviction path (docs/self-hosting/sleep.mdx:53-55 tells operators to set INSTA_OSS_MEM_BUDGET_MB) and it contradicts docs/self-hosting/sleep.mdx:45-48 (\"sleeps the least recently active running service, one at a time, until it is back above the floor\").
fix: Account for what has been freed inside the loop instead of trusting the runtime to notice. In evictForRoom keep a `let freed = 0`, test `if (mem.availableBytes + freed - needBytes >= floor) return` (line 461), and after a successful `await this.sleep(victim.key, 'memory')` add `if (ok) freed += this.rec(victim.key).lastRssBytes ?? DEFAULT_RSS[victim.kind]` (line 477 already has the boolean). Optionally also have DockerRuntime keep the per-container sample from the last stats() and subtract it from `lastRssTotal` in `stop()`, so budget mode self-corrects between passes.

problem: The sweep evaluates the idle rule once per pass but then stops candidates in sequential batches of four, each awaiting a docker stop that can burn the full grace (10 s compute, 30 s db). sleep() re-reads only the container state under the lock, never `lastActiveAt`, so a service that answers a request while an earlier batch is still stopping is stopped anyway and its in-flight request is dropped. Nothing else covers this case: a running service is dialled directly without a wake, so no op or wake ever appears in `busy()` and only the ledger stamp moves.
evidence: src/scheduler.ts:378-384 (`const now = Date.now()`, one `filter(isIdleCandidate(t, now))`, then `for (... i += SLEEP_CONCURRENCY) await Promise.all(...)`) and src/scheduler.ts:404-435 (the locked body re-reads `runtime.containers()` only; no stamp, holds or alwaysOn re-check). With 12 idle db candidates the third batch starts ~60 s after `now` was taken. Router side: src/router/http.ts:79-83 stamps and holds, then src/router/wake.ts:171 skips the wake entirely when `deps.stateOf(route) === 'running'`, so a live request on a batch-3 candidate leaves no trace the sweep looks at. Contract 00-contract.md:804 states the stamp condition as part of the sleep decision itself, not as a per-pass pre-filter.
fix: Re-assert freshness inside the lock, where the decision actually takes effect: in src/scheduler.ts:404 give sleep the target it already fetched and, right after `this.sleeping.add(key)` (line 412) and before the stop, bail with `false` when the reason is 'idle' and `!this.isIdleCandidate(t, Date.now())` (drop the `busy` clause from that call, since this key legitimately holds its own lock now), and when the reason is 'memory' and `this.holds(key) > 0 || Date.now() - this.rec(key).lastActiveAt < 2 * this.cfg.lanes.touchDebounceMs`. Cheapest correct variant: compute the guard inline from `this.rec(key).lastActiveAt`, `t.idleSec`, `t.alwaysOn`, `t.desiredState` and `this.holds(key)`.

problem: One failing docker stop aborts the whole sweep: the batch uses Promise.all, so a single rejected sleep() rejects the batch, skips every remaining idle candidate for that tick AND skips the pressure pass at the end of the sweep. The plan asks for the opposite (\"errors logged, retried next pass\"), and nothing logs the individual failure.
evidence: src/scheduler.ts:382-385 (`await Promise.all(candidates.slice(...).map((t) => this.sleep(t.key, 'idle')))` followed by `await this.evictForRoom(0, new Set())`; a rejection propagates out of sweep() to the tick handler at src/scheduler.ts:341-343, which logs one generic `warn: sleep sweep failed:` line). sleep() can reject: `runtime.containers()` (src/scheduler.ts:415) and `runtime.stop()` (src/scheduler.ts:429) both throw on a 20 s docker timeout (src/scheduler.ts:637-639). Plan 03 line 46: \"sleep(key, 'idle') oldest stamp first, concurrency 4; errors logged, retried next pass.\"
fix: Use `Promise.allSettled` for the batch at src/scheduler.ts:383 and log each rejection (`for (const r of results) if (r.status === 'rejected') console.warn(...)`), so a flaky stop costs one service on one tick instead of the rest of the pass and the memory-pressure pass.

problem: Every observability read forks a full `docker ps -a` before it decides anything: assertPgAwake calls scheduler.refreshStates() first. The contract declares that check as a synchronous, state-only test, and the dashboard polls the four routes it guards, so a box with many containers pays a process spawn plus a full container listing per poll per panel.
evidence: src/engine.ts:2479-2486 (`private async assertPgAwake(...) { await this.scheduler.refreshStates(); const live = this.stateOf(...) ... }`) called at src/engine.ts:1590, 1723, 1730, 1739; src/scheduler.ts:307-314 (`refreshStates` runs `runtime.containers()` = `docker ps -a`, src/scheduler.ts:585-593). Contract 00-contract.md:547 declares it `private assertPgAwake(project, branch, serviceId): void` (synchronous, throws), and plan 03 line 89 specifies only `stateOf(pgKey) !== 'running' -> throw`.
fix: Only pay for the docker read when the cheap answer would refuse: in src/engine.ts:2479 test `this.stateOf(key)` first, return when it is not 'asleep'/'starting', and only then `await this.scheduler.refreshStates()` and re-test before throwing. Correctness is unchanged (a snapshot is still confirmed before any refusal) and the common awake path costs nothing.

problem: Shutdown can now outlast the compose stop grace: after the lanes stop, main.ts awaits an in-flight sweep with no bound, and that sweep may be holding up to four docker stops with a 30 s database grace each. Blowing the 30 s stop_grace_period means SIGKILL, which skips releaseLock() and leaves the replacement container refusing the lock, which is the exact failure the surrounding comment says the ordering exists to prevent.
evidence: src/main.ts:178-185 (`await engine.scheduler.stop()` then `await Promise.race([app.close(), sleep(10_000)])`, comment at 165-168) and src/scheduler.ts:328-332 (`stop()` awaits `this.sweepInFlight` with no timeout); the sweep's stops use `graceFor` = stopGraceDbSec 30 s for databases (src/scheduler.ts:429, 439-442) with a docker timeout of 20 s + grace (src/scheduler.ts:637-639). install.sh:286 sets `stop_grace_period: 30s`.
fix: Bound the wait the way app.close() is bounded: `await Promise.race([engine.scheduler.stop(), sleep(5_000)])` at src/main.ts:181. `stop()` clears the interval and sets `stopped` synchronously, so the bound only shortens how long the daemon waits for a stop that docker will finish on its own anyway.

problem: WP3 changed three existing assertions in test/server.test.ts where its plan lists exactly one allowed edit. None is weakened, but two are unlisted, so the integration record does not say why the suite moved.
evidence: Plan 03 line 135 lists one edit (\"lines 475-489 expect state: 'stopped'\"), and only that one is in the plan. `git diff 50f729a~1 HEAD -- test/server.test.ts` also changes: `expect(db.runtime).toBe('stopped')` -> `'online'` (services row, now reading the one FakeRuntime store) and the `GET /projects/:id/database/instance` host assertion `'io-demo-main-pg'` -> `'127.0.0.1'` plus a port match (dbInstance switched to `this.laneAddress(...)` at src/engine.ts:1400), including the `?group=analytics` variant, which keeps its service identity pinned via the added `routeKey`.
fix: No code change: both edits are correct and contract-backed (decision 53 for the runtime column, 00-contract.md:717 \"lane host/port\" for database/instance). Record them in plan 03's Tests section next to the listed 475-489 edit before the integrator reads the diff, so the \"exactly one allowed edit\" claim matches the tree.

problem: `INSTA_OSS_RAM_FLOOR_PCT=0` is rejected at boot, so the one Docker suite WP3 wrote for the integrator and both public e2e scripts cannot run at all. loadConfig enforces a minimum of 1, but decision 12 requires 0 for exactly those runs and the docs advertise 0 as the off switch.
evidence: src/config.ts:247 `ramFloorPct: int(env, 'INSTA_OSS_RAM_FLOOR_PCT', 15, 1, 90)` with the thrower at src/config.ts:123. Proven: `npx tsx -e \"loadConfig({INSTA_OSS_RAM_FLOOR_PCT:'0'},[])\"` -> `INSTA_OSS_RAM_FLOOR_PCT must be an integer in 1..90 (got \"0\")`. Consumers that pass 0: test/sleep-wake.int.test.ts:43 (inside a module-scope `loadConfig`, so the file fails at collection, not in a test), e2e/local-smoke.sh:37 and e2e/server-smoke.sh:38 (`INSTA_OSS_RAM_FLOOR_PCT=${INSTA_OSS_RAM_FLOOR_PCT:-0}`, exported at line 39/40, so instad exits 1 before listening). Required by plans/impl/00-contract.md:81 and :853 (decision 12) and plans/impl/03-scheduler.md:143. Documented as the off switch at docs/self-hosting/sleep.mdx:115 and e2e/README.md:35. The contract's own config block contradicts its decision 12 at plans/impl/00-contract.md:189 (\"15 (1..90)\").
fix: src/config.ts:247 -> `int(env, 'INSTA_OSS_RAM_FLOOR_PCT', 15, 0, 90)`. Add `if (this.cfg.sleep.ramFloorPct <= 0) return` as the first line of `evictForRoom` (src/scheduler.ts:453) so 0 disables wake-time eviction too (the sweep's pass already no-ops: it calls `evictForRoom(0, ...)` and src/scheduler.ts:461 then compares `available - 0 >= 0`). Add a case beside test/config.test.ts:88 asserting `loadConfig({INSTA_OSS_RAM_FLOOR_PCT:'0'}).sleep.ramFloorPct === 0`, and change plans/impl/00-contract.md:189 to `15 (0..90; 0 disables the pressure pass)`.

problem: `GET /secrets` and the deploy env still emit container-internal DSNs: WP2's lane rewrite is applied only by `credentials`. Contract section 10 requires one host-facing string across secrets, credentials and env, and the README documents the lane form for `insta secrets --print`, which the daemon never produces. A developer who runs `insta secrets --print` or `insta secrets -o .env` gets `postgres://...@io-demo-main-pg-db:5432/app` (and `redis://...@io-demo-main-rd-cache:6379/0`), which does not resolve from the host in either mode.
evidence: src/engine.ts:2647-2657 `dbSecretsFor` writes `row.url` verbatim; src/engine.ts:578-581 `managedSecretsFor` builds the bundle from `managedContainerName(...)`; both feed `mintedSecretsFor` (src/engine.ts:561-564) which is what `secrets()` (src/engine.ts:552-556) and `envFor()` (src/engine.ts:2714-2722) return, while `credentialsOn` correctly goes through `laneUrl` (src/engine.ts:2733). Measured on the fake engine: server mode `GET /secrets?branch=main` -> `DATABASE_URL=postgres://postgres:pw@io-demo-main-pg-db:5432/app` while `GET /services/pg-db/credentials` -> `postgres://postgres:pw@pg-db-demo-main.example.test:5432/app?sslmode=require`; local mode secrets -> `io-demo-main-pg-db:5432`, credentials -> `127.0.0.1:20000`. problem: The sleep page overstates the post-wake retry budget by 8 seconds.
evidence: docs/self-hosting/sleep.mdx:68-69 \"held while the container starts, for up to 60 seconds, plus up to 38 seconds of readiness retries after that\". The real second budget is `INSTA_OSS_READY_WINDOW_MS`, default 30000 (src/config.ts:230, declared at src/config.ts:49), consumed once per woken request at src/router/http.ts:92 (`retryUntil = woke ? Date.now() + cfg.lanes.readyWindowMs : 0`) and enforced at src/router/http.ts:203. The first 60 s is `INSTA_OSS_WAKE_TIMEOUT_SEC` (src/scheduler.ts:552-557), which already contains the readiness polling rather than preceding it.
fix: docs/self-hosting/sleep.mdx:69 -> \"plus up to 30 seconds of readiness retries after that\", and add `INSTA_OSS_READY_WINDOW_MS | 30000 | retry window for a just-woken upstream` to the tuning table at docs/self-hosting/sleep.mdx:106-118.
